rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Objective 3 How to Play 3.1 1. Flip 3.2 2. Check Fame 3.3 3. Market 3.3.1 Hire a Toon 3.3.2 Dismiss a Toon 3.4 4. Refill the Market 3.5 5. Cleanup 4 Final Flip Overview You are a top talent agent in charge of hiring actors for the next great show. Choose from the many colorful characters in Flip Valley to make the perfect cast. FlipToons is a deckbuilding game where each player buys cards that increase their chances of gaining fame points when laid out on a grid. Fame points allow you to buy better cards and get rid of bad cards. Objective Once any player reaches 30 fame, all players compare casts in a Final Flip. The player with the highest number of fame points wins. SOLO: Reach 30 Fame during a Check Fame phase before the Deck runs out (the deck is 30/27/24 cards (easy/normal/hard) after the market setup). How to Play Each player's turn consists of 5 phases. 1. Flip At the beginning of a round, each player flips cards into a 3x2 grid from left to right, top to bottom. Some card abilities change their worth or how many cards are placed and where. 2. Check Fame Each Toon in the grid is evaluated for how much fame they have generated. Fame is marked to the left of the grid. If any player generated 30 or more points The player who initiated the Final Flip gets the "critic's choice" award, which adds 3 points to their Final Flip total. 3. Market A player can make up to two actions, either two of the same, one of each, or only one, or skip all. Hire a Toon Each Toon in the market has a "fame price" above it. Higher ranking Toons are more expensive. Spend earned fame on one Toon, which is placed on top of the deck. Dismiss a Toon Choose a Toon revealed in the player's grid. That card is removed from the game by spending 5 fame points and does not go back into the player's deck at any time. This action cannot be taken if the player has four or less cards in their deck. Fame is not recalculated. Note: Unspent fame does not carry over to the next round. 4. Refill the Market If there are fewer than 5 cards in the market, cards are revealed from the Toon deck to replace them. Cards are then rearranged according to rank. This may mean any given card may be a lower or higher price for the next player. If the market is ever depleted, the Final Flip is instantiated. 5. Cleanup All cards in each player's grid are collected back into their deck. The decks are then reshuffled. (In two-player games, the leftmost and rightmost cards in the market are discarded, then refilled.) The "first player" token is passed to the next player. If any player generated at least 30 fame in the previous "Check Fame" phase, players proceed to the Final Flip. Otherwise, a new round starts. If playing with solo/two players, the leftmost and rightmost cards in the market are discarded, refilled and rearranged by rank. Final Flip All players complete one last flip phase and check fame phase. The player who generated the Final Flip gets an additional 3 fame for their "Critic's Choice" award. The player who generates the most fame has assembled the best cast of characters and wins.

[Rating: 1/10] Kind of a bad deckbuilder. Well everyone in the comments is saying it's also an auto-battler, but aren't they pretty much the same thing? Choosing the order to play cards was an illusion in most deckbuilders anyway. What's annoying is that it's more work than thrill, calculating numbers and adding them up based on a grid. I really don't mind randomness, but nothing exciting happens here. Or interactive, since you rarely care about others' [i]tableaus[/i].  The old timey cartoon art feels so bland. [Rating: 1/10] Bland deck builder—a genre/mechanism to which I’m often allergic—made worse by the randomness, extreme card asymmetry, and brevity of the game. That brevity is by design (I think) but proper deck building either needs more time to be effective, or, uh, other "things" to prop it up (e.g. see: LOST RUINS OF ARNAK). This is filler for the sake of filler and it isn't particularly fun or clever filler at that. Bleh.

[Rating: 2/10] Off-the charts randomness is not a good bedfellow for a deck-builder where you spend a significant chunk of your VP on buying cards.

[Rating: 2/10] Hard to believe this game out in 2025. There are no decisions to be made except which card to buy. Extremely luck-dependent.

[Rating: 3/10] Pure luck.  There are almost no decisions in this game.  You just randomly flip over your cards and see what happens.  Thankfully the game is only like 15 minutes long, which is why I didn't rate it lower.

[Rating: 3/10] Very random deck builder.  It has some cool ideas, with everyone flipping their "hand" of 6 cards simultaneously and being able to spend money to either buy cards or trash cards. But in practice it pretty much sucks. I like the idea of new cards entering the market slotting into a cost slot relative to their value, rather than a sliding market where new card go in the most expensive slot, but by mid game the market is full of cards no one wants and they can afford to buy the most expensive cards anyway.
